author: Jim Mishler
title: Federal Judge Declines Request to Block Trump Administration's Takeover of USIP
text:
• A federal judge has declined a request by leaders of the U.S. Institute of Peace (USIP) to block the Trump administration's takeover of the nonprofit.
• U.S. District Judge Beryl Howell expressed alarm at the actions of representatives from Elon Musk's Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) during a hearing.
• Howell stated that fired board members likely have no standing to file in their official capacity.
• The judge was offended by DOGE staff's use of threats and law enforcement to gain access to USIP headquarters.
• DOGE staff removed USIP's president, George Moose, from the building on Monday.
• Howell declined to restore the former board members to their positions or bar DOGE staff from USIP's headquarters.
• Three law enforcement departments were present at USIP on Monday to assist DOGE workers.
• President Donald Trump issued an executive order last month targeting USIP and three other agencies for closure.
• USIP is a think tank created and funded by Congress in 1984, aimed at preventing and resolving conflicts.
• Board members of USIP are nominated by the president and must be confirmed by the Senate.
